_readme: For VD's panels. Generated from heat/data/city_series.json and city_nights.json
at commit 5499c20. Do not hand-edit.
TWO DAY SERIES, and they are different instruments. Do not mix them.
days_by_year_p90  above the city's own 90TH percentile, the hottest tenth.
VD's reader threshold: easier to hold, and the degrees are
a temperature a local recognises. NOT the one heat ranks on,
so NO RANK may appear beside it.
days_by_year_p95  above the city's own 95TH percentile. This IS the ranked
index. day_rank below belongs to THIS series and no other.
nights_by_year    nights at or above 20.0 C (ETCCDI TR). night_rank is on this.
warmest_night_c   the warmest single night of each year, in degrees. A PEAK,
not a count: it ranks differently and carries its own rank
or none. Paris is 1st on the day count and 2nd on its
hottest day, so a peak claim may never borrow a count rank.
Every series is counted TO THE SAME CALENDAR DAY each year, that city's own cut,
in `cut_at`. Thin years are omitted rather than sent as zero. 2026 is the last
entry of each array and appears exactly once.
ROUNDING: round what you DISPLAY, never compute from the rounded number.
Rounding the baseline would overstate the ratio in 9 of these 21 cities;
Marseille goes from 23.7x to 34x. See the rounding note in this project.
NIGHTS ARE GATED in Paris and Bilbao: about one a year is too thin a base for a
ratio. The series is here; do not draw a multiple from it.
